title: SEND THIS — three one-sheets you can text to a person
dek: How to add an MCP in one sitting, the AI tools actually on this desk, and where the money is in AI work. Each one has a plain-text twin you can paste into a message.
body:
Mike asked for utilities he could send to one person: how to set up an MCP, what AI tools are on the desk, ways to make capital with AI contributions. Three sheets now sit at /send, and each one is short enough to read on a phone while standing up.

Nothing on them is new. /send/mcp carries the four client recipes verbatim from /connectors plus the Cursor line, with this town's own endpoint as the worked example. /send/ai-tools lists thirty tools that appear somewhere in this repository, each with the page it shows up on and whether the cost is stated; where the repo says nothing about price, the sheet says so rather than guessing. /send/ai-capital distils the twenty-nine routes from the AI income field guide into seven lanes, then prints the three rails this town runs with their real numbers: the season ticket has recorded no tickets, x402 has settled no receipts, and the Tezos contracts hold twenty editions and three mugs. The rails are live and the money is thin.

Every sheet has three bodies: the page, a JSON twin, and a plain-text twin at the same address with .txt on the end. The text is what you paste into a message. There is a copy button for the impatient and a text-it link for the phone.
